glosses.notes: Used for testing or examining machines, health conditions, products, or data to see whether something is normal, safe, or working properly.

examples.sentence: 医院那边人很多，医生先让他去做检测，不是因为情况已经特别严重，而是想在用药以前把身体里真正的问题查清楚。
火车站准备开门以前，工作人员先把机器全检测一遍，怕等到人一多的时候，门口突然出问题，大家就都堵在外面。
新桥开放以前，负责的人连续几天在夜里检测最容易出问题的地方，因为白天车太多，很多细小的变化反而看不出来。

example_translations.translation: There were many people at the hospital, and the doctor first sent him to get testing done, not because the situation was already especially serious, but because he wanted to find out the real problem in the body before giving medicine.
Before the station opened its doors, the staff first examined all the machines once, worried that if something suddenly went wrong when the crowd grew, everyone would be stuck outside the entrance.

Before the new bridge opened, the people in charge spent several nights in a row testing the places most likely to have problems, because in the daytime there were too many cars and many small changes were actually hard to notice.

glosses.notes: Means to make something simpler by reducing steps, details, or rules so people can understand or do it more easily.

examples.sentence: 把报名过程简化以后，来的人虽然还是很多，但是大家不用再一层一层地问，所以前面的队也走得快多了。
老师怕第一次来的人听不懂，就先把最难的部分简化成几个小问题，让大家一步一步地想，不要一开始就被吓住。
公司这次不是想省事而已，而是想把太复杂的流程简化，因为同一件小事要是总让人来回跑，最后连负责的人也记不清。

example_translations.translation: After the registration process was simplified, there were still many people coming, but everyone no longer had to ask about things step by step, so the line in front moved much faster.

The teacher was afraid the people coming for the first time would not understand, so she first simplified the hardest part into several small questions, letting everyone think through them step by step instead of feeling overwhelmed at the very start.

This time the company was not merely trying to save trouble. It wanted to simplify an overly complicated process, because if the same small matter keeps making people run back and forth, even the person in charge eventually cannot keep it all straight.

glosses.notes: Can mean a short introduction in written form, or the act of briefly introducing a person, place, plan, or topic.

examples.sentence: 会议开始以前，主持人先用几分钟简介了一下来的人和今天要谈的事情，免得后面有人刚坐下就听不明白。
墙上那张学校简介写得不长，但是把这几年最重要的变化都说到了，所以不少家长站在前面看了很久才进去。
导游没有一上来就讲很多过去的事，先让大家看墙上的简介，再让第一次来的人知道自己现在到底在哪个地方。

example_translations.translation: Before the meeting began, the host spent a few minutes briefly introducing the people present and what would be discussed that day, so that no one would sit down and immediately feel lost.
The school introduction posted on the wall was not long, but it covered the most important changes of the past few years, so quite a few parents stood in front of it for a long time before going in.

The guide did not start by talking about many things from the past. He first let everyone read the introduction on the wall, and then helped the people visiting for the first time understand exactly where they were.

glosses.notes: Means to become weaker or to make something weaker in strength, effect, sound, pain, or influence.

examples.sentence: 风到了半夜终于开始减弱，前面一直怕窗会开的人这才把灯关掉，但是谁也没有马上睡着。
医生说药吃下去以后，疼不会一下子全消失，但是要是到了明天还一点也没有减弱，就得再回来让他看看。
这件事在网上刚出来的时候声音很大，后来因为更多细节慢慢说清楚了，大家的误会才一点一点减弱。

example_translations.translation: The wind finally began to weaken after midnight, and only then did the people who had been afraid the window might fly open turn off the light, though no one fell asleep right away.

The doctor said that after the medicine was taken, the pain would not disappear all at once, but if it had not weakened even a little by tomorrow, the patient would need to come back and let him take another look.
When this matter first appeared online, the reaction was loud, but later, as more details were gradually explained clearly, people’s misunderstanding only then slowly diminished.

glosses.notes: Used for reducing physical pressure or, more often in everyday speech, easing mental stress so someone feels less burdened.

examples.sentence: 老师让大家先做几分钟呼吸，不是为了表演什么新方法，而是想在考试以前帮全班减压，让手心别一直出汗。
医院门口新开那间小屋子专门给家里的人减压，里面没有什么复杂安排，只是让人先坐下喝口水，再把心里怕的事慢慢说出来。
朋友知道他最近事情太多，就约他周末早点出门爬山，说与其一直把话压在心里，不如先看看风景减压，再回去想怎么办。

example_translations.translation: The teacher asked everyone to spend a few minutes breathing first, not to show off any new method, but to help the whole class relieve pressure before the exam so their palms would stop sweating.

The little room newly opened by the hospital entrance is specially for helping family members relieve pressure. There is nothing complicated inside; people are simply asked to sit down, drink some water, and then slowly say what they are afraid of.

Knowing he had too much going on lately, his friend invited him to go hiking early on the weekend, saying that instead of keeping everything bottled up, it would be better to look at the scenery first, relieve some pressure, and then go back and think about what to do.

glosses.notes: Used for inspecting, testing, or proving whether a method, product, ability, or judgment can really stand up in practice.

examples.sentence: 真正能检验这套办法有没有用的，不是会议上说得多漂亮，而是下个月人一多的时候，前面会不会还是一样乱。
老师常说，考试只能检验学生记住了多少东西，但是不一定能看出他会不会把这些东西拿来用。
这次长途路最能检验那辆旧车的不是白天平路，而是夜里上山以后，灯和刹车还能不能一直稳定。

example_translations.translation: What can truly test whether this method works is not how nicely it is described in a meeting, but whether things will still be just as chaotic next month when there are many more people.
The teacher often says that exams can only test how much students have memorized, but they do not necessarily show whether a student can actually use what has been learned.
What best tests that old car on this long journey is not the flat road in daylight, but whether the lights and brakes can stay stable after going uphill at night.

glosses.notes: Refers to a sword, often in historical, performance, decorative, or martial-arts settings rather than everyday life.

examples.sentence: 博物馆那把旧剑放在玻璃后面看着不算特别大，但是导游一讲到它当年怎么跟着主人走了很远，前面的人一下子都安静了。
他小时候看戏最喜欢看将军手里的剑，长大以后再回去看，才发现真正让人记住的不是动作快，大家记住的是台上那种感觉。
店里卖给游客的小剑看上去很亮，但是老师还是提醒学生先看墙上的字，因为那些话更能让人明白那个时代的人怎么想。

example_translations.translation: That old sword in the museum did not look especially large behind the glass, but the moment the guide talked about how far it had once traveled with its owner, the people in front suddenly fell silent.

When he was little, what he liked most in opera was looking at the sword in the general’s hand. Only after growing up and going back to watch again did he realize that what people truly remembered was not the speed of the movement, but the feeling on stage.

The little swords sold to visitors in the shop looked very shiny, but the teacher still reminded the students to read the words on the wall first, because those words reveal more clearly how people of that era thought.

glosses.notes: Refers to an arrow in archery, hunting, or symbolic scenes, and it often appears with verbs like 射, 拉, or 指向.

examples.sentence: 练习的时候，教练没有先让新来的人比谁射得远，而是一直提醒大家看清每一支箭出去以前手有没有乱动。
山路口那块旧牌子上的箭被太阳晒得有点淡了，第一次来的司机差点开错方向，后来还是靠路边的人提醒才停下来。
电影里那一箭飞出去的时候，全场一下子都安静了，但是导演后来解释说，真正难拍的不是箭本身，大家等那一刻的表情才最难拍。

example_translations.translation: During practice, the coach did not first make the newcomers compete over whose shot went farther. Instead, he kept reminding everyone to watch carefully whether the hand moved around before each arrow went out.

The arrow on that old sign at the mountain road entrance had faded a bit under the sun, and the driver visiting for the first time almost went the wrong way, only stopping because someone by the roadside reminded him.

When that arrow flew out in the film, the whole audience went silent at once, but the director later explained that what was hardest to shoot was not the arrow itself, but the expressions on people’s faces as they waited for that moment.

glosses.notes: Can mean professionally identifying or appraising something, and it also refers to the resulting expert evaluation.

examples.sentence: 那幅画送去鉴定以前，家里人谁也不敢把话说满，因为大家都知道，光看外面旧不旧，还不能说明它到底值不值钱。
医院让他先做一份鉴定，不是为了把事情闹大，只是怕以后真要说清责任的时候，手里一点根据都没有。
老师把两块看起来很像的石头拿来给学生看，先让大家自己猜，再讲为什么真正的鉴定不能只靠颜色，还得看里面的成分。

example_translations.translation: Before the painting was sent out for appraisal, no one in the family dared speak too confidently, because everyone knew that judging only by whether the outside looked old could not show whether it was actually valuable.

The hospital asked him to get an appraisal first, not to make the matter bigger, but because they feared that if responsibility truly had to be clarified later, he would have no evidence in hand at all.

The teacher brought two stones that looked very similar for the students to look at, let everyone guess first, and then explained why real identification cannot rely only on color and must also look at what is inside.

glosses.notes: Refers to the time or space between things, and it can also mean keeping things apart rather than packed together.

examples.sentence: 这几班车白天的间隔本来就不长，不过一下雨路上又慢，所以站里的人越来越多，后面来的人只能一直往外站。
医生看了他的记录以后，说药还是要继续吃，但是每次吃药的间隔最好固定一点，不要今天早明天晚，这样身体更容易乱。
这排树看上去长得差不多，其实种的时候就故意留了间隔，因为要是靠得太近，过几年以后谁也长不好。

example_translations.translation: The interval between these buses during the day is not long to begin with, but once it rains the road slows down, so more and more people build up in the station and those who come later can only keep standing farther out.

After looking at his records, the doctor said the medicine still had to be taken, but the interval between each dose should ideally be more fixed and not early one day and late the next, because that only makes the body more unsettled.

These rows of trees look as if they all grew in much the same way, but when they were planted, gaps were intentionally left between them, because if they stand too close together, after a few years none of them will grow well.

glosses.notes: Describes something that happens through another step, person, or effect rather than in a direct way.

examples.sentence: 他虽然没有直接说反对，但是那句听上去很轻的话其实已经间接告诉大家，这个计划再往前走就会出更大的问题。
这次停电看起来只是小事，但是它间接影响了整栋楼的工作安排，连原来不需要改时间的会议最后也只好往后推。
她没有上台，但是后来很多人都说，那份提前发下来的说明其实间接帮了大忙，因为不少人正是看了它才听懂后面的内容。

example_translations.translation: Although he did not directly say he opposed it, that lightly spoken sentence had already indirectly told everyone that this plan would lead to even bigger problems if it kept moving forward.

This power outage looked like a small matter, but it indirectly affected the work arrangements of the whole building, and even the meeting that originally did not need its time changed had to be pushed back in the end.

She did not go on stage, but later many people said that the explanation handed out in advance had actually helped in an indirect but important way, because many people understood the later content only after reading it.

glosses.notes: Can describe something as sound and complete, such as a system or mind, and it can also mean improving something to make it more complete.

examples.sentence: 老师说一个班风气是不是健全，不能只看前面几个成绩最好的学生，还要看平时最安静的人有困难的时候会不会有人去帮。
这套制度现在还谈不上多健全，所以负责人每隔一段时间就要把大家叫回来问一遍，看看还有没有谁总是在同一个地方吃亏。
医生检查完以后说，孩子身体还是健全的，家里人这才松了口气，不过后面该注意的地方还是一样不能少。

example_translations.translation: The teacher said that whether the atmosphere of a class is sound cannot be judged only by looking at the few students with the best grades; one must also see whether anyone will help the quietest students when they run into difficulties.

This system still cannot be called very complete, so the person in charge has to call everyone back from time to time and ask through things again, to see whether there is still anyone who keeps losing out in the same place.

After the examination, the doctor said the child’s body was still sound overall, and only then did the family feel relieved, though the things that needed attention afterward still could not be ignored.

glosses.notes: Refers to a physical building or structure, often when talking about cities, campuses, safety, or historical sites.

examples.sentence: 这片老街最吸引人的不只是那几座高大的建筑物，大家更容易记住的是它们前后靠得很近，站在中间往上看时，人会一下子忘了外面的新路有多宽。
下雨那天大家先跑进旁边的建筑物里躲一躲，后来才发现里面墙上的旧照片正好把这条街过去最热闹的时候都留了下来。
学校带学生去看那些老建筑物，不是只想让大家知道名字，而是想让他们看看，一个城市把什么留下来，其实就是在说明它重视什么。

example_translations.translation: What draws people most to this old street is not only those few tall buildings. What people remember more easily is how closely they stand in front of and behind one another, so that when you look up from the middle, you suddenly forget how wide the new roads outside are.

On the rainy day, everyone first ran into the nearby building to shelter for a while, and only later discovered that the old photographs on the wall had happened to preserve the busiest period in the street’s past.
The school took the students to see those old buildings not only to let them know the names, but to let them see that what a city chooses to keep is in fact a way of showing what it values.

glosses.notes: Refers to a military general, often in historical, dramatic, or symbolic scenes about leadership and responsibility.

examples.sentence: 戏台上那位将军一出场，下面的孩子就都不说话了，但是老人后来说，真正像样的不是衣服多重，而是眼神一抬就让人信了。
博物馆里那封信写得并不长，却让很多人第一次看见，一位将军在夜里也会怕第二天出去的人回不来。
电影把那位老将军拍得很安静，他很少大声发命令，但是越到后面大家越明白，真正让人服气的是他一直把别人放在前面。

example_translations.translation: The moment that general appeared on stage, all the children below fell silent, but later an old man said that what truly made the role convincing was not how heavy the costume was, but how one lift of the eyes made people believe.
That letter in the museum was not long, but it let many people see for the first time that even a general would fear at night that the people going out the next day might not return.

The film portrayed that old general as very quiet. He rarely gave orders loudly, yet the further the story went, the more everyone understood that what truly earned respect was that he always put others first.

glosses.notes: Means to explain something carefully and clearly, often to students, visitors, or people seeing a process for the first time.

examples.sentence: 导游在前面讲解的时候，没有急着把所有年份一口气都说完，而是先让大家看看墙上的图，再慢慢把最重要的变化连起来。
老师知道这一页最难，所以特意把讲解分成几步，先问一个小问题，再带大家往后想，这样后排原来走神的人也跟上了。
机器刚打开的时候声音有点大，但是负责讲解的人还是站在旁边一点一点地说，因为他知道不少第一次来的人光看动作根本看不懂。

example_translations.translation: While the guide was explaining at the front, he did not rush to say all the dates in one breath. Instead, he first let everyone look at the pictures on the wall, and then slowly connected the most important changes.

The teacher knew this page was the hardest, so she deliberately divided the explanation into several steps, first asking one small question and then leading everyone forward, so that even the people in the back who had originally lost focus were able to catch up.

When the machine was first turned on, the sound was rather loud, but the person responsible for explaining still stood to one side and spoke little by little, because he knew many first-time visitors could not understand it at all by only watching the movements.

glosses.notes: Refers to a medal won in a competition or awarded in recognition of achievement.

examples.sentence: 她把那块奖牌放好以后，家里人先没有去问名次，大家都想知道，她在那么冷的天里到底怎么一个人把最后那段路坚持完的。
她回来的那天，最先摸那块奖牌的不是记者，而是那几个平时一起练到最晚的人，因为只有他们最清楚这一路有多不容易。
博物馆把旧奖牌和照片放在一起，不是为了让人只看谁赢了，而是想让年轻人明白，那一代人把机会拿到手有多难。

example_translations.translation: After she put that medal down properly, the family did not first ask about her ranking. What everyone wanted to know was how she had managed to push through the final stretch alone in weather that cold.

On the day she returned, the first people to touch that medal were not the reporters, but the few people who usually trained alongside her latest into the day, because only they truly knew how difficult the road had been.

The museum placed old medals and photographs together not to make people focus only on who had won, but to help young people understand how difficult it had been for that generation to obtain their opportunities.

glosses.notes: Refers to a prize given for winning a contest, answering correctly, or taking part in an event.

examples.sentence: 活动快结束的时候，主持人把最后一份奖品举得很高，但是台下的人最开心的并不是它值多少钱，大家更在意自己刚才是不是真的答对了最难那题。
老师这次准备的奖品不算贵，但是每一样都跟书和画有关，所以就连原来只想来看热闹的孩子，后来也认真坐到最后。
店里为了吸引路过的人，把奖品放在门口最亮的地方，但是老板心里也明白，要是里面的东西不好，光靠这个办法留不住客人。

example_translations.translation: As the event was drawing to a close, the host held the last prize high, but what made the people below happiest was not how much it was worth. They cared more about whether they had really answered the hardest question correctly just then.

The prizes the teacher prepared this time were not expensive, but each one had to do with books and painting, so even children who had originally come only to watch the excitement sat seriously through to the end.
To attract people passing by, the shop put the prize in the brightest place by the door, but the owner also knew that if the things inside were not good, this trick alone could not keep customers.

glosses.notes: Usually refers to a thick sauce or paste used in cooking, and it can also appear in cooking verbs meaning to coat something with sauce.

examples.sentence: 厨房里那锅肉还没完全好，做饭的人先吃了一点，说酱现在还不够厚，要是再急着关火，吃起来就只剩咸味没有香味了。
他小时候最怕饭里那种黑黑的酱，长大以后陪朋友去老店再吃，才明白原来好不好吃，差的不是颜色，差的是后面慢慢出来的香味。
这家店做鱼以前会先把酱调好，不是为了让动作看起来专业，而是因为火一开大以后，再去找这个找那个就来不及了。

example_translations.translation: The pot of meat in the kitchen was not fully ready yet, so the person doing the cooking ate a little first and said the sauce was still not thick enough. If the fire was turned off too quickly now, it would taste salty but not fragrant.

When he was little, he disliked that black sauce in rice dishes the most. Only after growing up and going with friends to eat at the old shop again did he understand that what made it good or bad was not the color, but the fragrance that slowly came out afterward.

Before cooking fish, this shop first prepares the sauce properly, not to make the process look professional, but because once the fire is turned high, there is no time to keep searching around for things.

glosses.notes: Refers to soy sauce, a common dark seasoning used in Chinese cooking for color, saltiness, and depth of flavor.

examples.sentence: 母亲站在锅边看了一会儿，说先别急着再放酱油，因为汤已经收得差不多了，现在颜色刚好，再多一点味道就会压住菜本身。
他第一次给那么多人做饭，最怕的不是火太大，而是手一紧张就把酱油倒多了，所以旁边的人一直提醒他先少一点再慢慢看。
小店里那瓶老酱油摆在最里面，看上去一点也不特别，但是老板一开盖，很多站在门口的人就都知道，这碗面最后的味道大半要靠它。

example_translations.translation: The mother stood by the pot and watched for a while, then said not to hurry to add more soy sauce, because the soup had already reduced almost enough, the color was just right, and any more would overpower the dish itself.

It was his first time cooking for so many people, and what he feared most was not that the fire would be too high, but that in his nervousness he would pour too much soy sauce, so the person beside him kept reminding him to add a little first and then look again slowly.

That old bottle of soy sauce sat at the very back of the little shop and looked nothing special, but the moment the owner opened the lid, many people standing by the doorway understood that the final flavor of the noodles would depend mostly on it.

glosses.notes: Refers to adhesive tape used to seal, stick, wrap, or temporarily fix something in place.

examples.sentence: 最下面那一层胶带要是没贴紧，车一开远就容易散，所以他们装完最后一件东西以后，又蹲在门口从头检查了一遍。
医生换药的时候，先慢慢把旧胶带一点一点拿下来，怕动作一快就又碰到伤口，所以旁边看的人都不敢随便说话。
雨刚停的时候，窗边还有风进来，父亲先拿胶带临时贴住，不是觉得这样就算修好了，而是想等明天白天再仔细处理。

example_translations.translation: If the bottom layer of tape is not stuck down tightly, it easily comes apart once the vehicle goes far, so after loading the final item they squatted by the door and checked everything all over again.

When the doctor changed the dressing, he first slowly took the old tape off little by little, worried that moving too quickly would touch the wound again, so the people nearby did not dare speak carelessly.

Just after the rain stopped, wind was still coming in by the window, so the father first used tape to stick it shut temporarily, not because he thought that counted as fixing it, but because he wanted to deal with it carefully in daylight the next day.

glosses.notes: Refers to the central point that attention gathers around in a discussion, event, conflict, image, or relationship.

examples.sentence: 记者到了现场以后才发现，大家争了半天的焦点并不是钱够不够，而是这件事以后到底由谁来真正负责。
这场讨论原来快散了，但是他最后一句话一下子把焦点又拉了回来，因为所有人都意识到，前面一直没有人正面回答那个最关键的问题。
电影前半段看起来像在讲家庭小事，但是看到后面大家才明白，真正的焦点一直是每个人心里那份说不出来的亏欠。

example_translations.translation: Only after arriving on the scene did the reporter discover that the focus of everyone’s long argument was not whether there was enough money, but who would truly be responsible for the matter afterward.
The discussion had been about to end, but his final sentence suddenly pulled the focus back, because everyone realized that no one had directly answered the most crucial question earlier.
The first half of the film looked as if it were about small family matters, but later everyone understood that the real focus had always been the unspoken sense of guilt in each person’s heart.

glosses.notes: Refers to dealing with people in social settings, especially the skill of communicating and getting along with others in a natural way.

examples.sentence: 她工作不算最早，但是因为交际方面一直很自然，所以每次有新同事来，负责人总愿意先让她带着去见人。
老师提醒学生，学一门外语不能只看考试分数，因为真到了要和别人来往的时候，没有一点交际能力，很多话懂了也还是开不了口。
他年轻时最怕人多的地方，后来慢慢出来做事才发现，交际不是一定要把每句话都说得漂亮，先学会认真听别人到底在怕什么更重要。

example_translations.translation: She was not among the earliest employees, but because she had always been natural in social interaction, the person in charge was always willing to let her take new coworkers around to meet people first.

The teacher reminded the students that when learning a foreign language, they cannot focus only on exam scores, because when the time truly comes to deal with other people, without any social ability they may understand a great deal and still be unable to speak.

When he was young he feared crowded places most, and only later, after gradually entering work and society, did he realize that socializing does not mean saying every sentence beautifully. What matters more is first learning to listen carefully to what others are really afraid of.

glosses.notes: Describes feeling anxious, uneasy, or mentally strained, often over uncertainty, pressure, or fear of what might happen next.

examples.sentence: 结果还没出来以前，家里人谁都不敢把话说满，所以大家一直都很安静，连平时最不容易焦虑的那个人也不停地去门口看时间。
她知道一直想最坏的结果只会让自己更焦虑，但是事情真正落到眼前的时候，手心还是会先出汗，话也比平时少很多。
医生后来提醒他说，身体已经很累的时候，再让自己长期焦虑，最先出问题的往往不是心情，而是吃饭和睡觉都慢慢乱掉。

example_translations.translation: Before the result came out, no one in the family dared speak too confidently, so everyone stayed very quiet, and even the person who normally felt anxious least easily kept going to the doorway to check the time.

She knew that constantly imagining the worst result would only make her more anxious, but when the matter truly arrived before her eyes, her palms still began to sweat first and she spoke far less than usual.

The doctor later reminded him that when the body is already very tired, if he lets himself stay anxious for a long time, the first things to go wrong are often not the emotions themselves, but eating and sleeping, both of which slowly become disordered.

glosses.notes: Refers to liquid glue used for sticking paper, wood, fabric, or small handmade objects together.

examples.sentence: 孩子把作业本弄破以后，本来想随便倒点胶水粘上就算了，但是老师看见以后还是让他重新贴好，因为明天还要交给全班的人看。
做模型的时候，最麻烦的不是缺零件，而是胶水一多就容易流出来，所以那位老师傅每次都只肯先点一点，再慢慢等它干。
她后来找到小时候做的手工，上面的胶水早就变黄了，但是那些歪歪扭扭的边还在，一看就知道当年做的人有多认真。

example_translations.translation: After the child tore the workbook, he originally wanted to pour on some glue and be done with it, but after seeing it the teacher still told him to paste it back properly, because it still had to be shown to the whole class the next day.

When making models, the most troublesome part is not lacking pieces, but that if there is too much glue it easily runs out, so that old craftsman is only willing to dab on a little each time and then slowly wait for it to dry.

Later she found a craft she had made as a child. The glue on it had long since turned yellow, but the crooked edges were still there, and one glance made it clear how serious the maker had been back then.

glosses.notes: Means to talk with someone in a calm, two-way way, often face to face about feelings, plans, or serious matters.

examples.sentence: 两个人原来只是站在门外等人，后来因为天气太冷才开始交谈，结果越说越觉得彼此想的事情很像，连时间都忘了看。
医生进门以前，家里人已经在外面小声交谈了很久，谁都想先把心里最怕的事说出来，免得一会儿真正见到医生又紧张得开不了口。
这位老人平时话不多，但是一有人坐下来认真跟他交谈，他就会把那些很多人早已经忘了的小事一件一件地慢慢说出来。

example_translations.translation: The two people had originally only been standing outside waiting for someone, but because the weather was so cold they began to talk, and as they continued, they increasingly felt that they were thinking about very similar things and even forgot to look at the time.

Before the doctor came in, the family had already been quietly talking outside for a long time. Everyone wanted to say the thing they feared most first, so that when they actually saw the doctor they would not become so nervous that they could not speak.
This old man does not usually say much, but once someone sits down and talks with him seriously, he slowly begins telling those small matters that many people have already forgotten, one by one.
